change.summary: Ran the PE stage of the build with the native Windows compiler rebuilt from the pinned tree, directly on the two committed snapshot stores. The 8-function executor artifact is byte-identical to the committed one. The 181-function server artifact has the same file size and passes the whole external suite, but is not byte-identical: the native backend omits the reference build's single Windows guard-page stack probe, which shifts the rest of the image by 16 bytes and changes 231 313 of 359 424 bytes. The reference author path (xax_build.build) still reproduces the committed 9f6e272b artifact exactly. The remaining B1 gap is therefore a specific native/self-hosted codegen omission, not the ability to run the stage natively.
change.correction: NATIVE.md previously said the native compiler cannot rebuild the committed program stores because they are decoder output, not build requests. The store root for both programs is a form-3 SNAPSHOT (the release request is a referenced object), so `xaxc build <store> <artifact> <prov>` consumes them directly. Only the seed store is a form-2 request and needs `resolve` first.

parity.interpretation: the images have the same container geometry, identical import data and the same code, with one structural difference: the reference image emits a Windows stack-probe sequence for the large frame at the start of the function at code offset 86,304, and the native image replaces it with one flat `sub rsp, 0x1d38`. That insertion shifts the rest of the image by 16 bytes after alignment, so a position-wise comparison reports 231 313 differing bytes even though the tail is 99.5% equal when compared under the shift; the remaining differences are relocation fields whose displacements changed. The probe pattern (`sub rsp, 0x1000; test byte [rsp], 0; sub rsp, 0xd38; test byte [rsp], 0`) occurs once in the author image and zero times in the native image (14 vs 13 `sub rsp, imm32` instructions). It is not a header, timestamp or path artifact: the PE timestamp and checksum are zero in both, and the native build is deterministic.

example.author_sequence: push rbx/rbp/rsi/rdi/r12-r15; sub rsp, 0x1000; test byte [rsp], 0; sub rsp, 0xd38; test byte [rsp], 0 (frame 0x1d38)
example.native_sequence: push rbx/rbp/rsi/rdi/r12-r15; sub rsp, 0x1d38 (no guard-page probe)

parity.not_claimed: the two images are not proven instruction-for-instruction equivalent or semantically identical, and the native image is not claimed to be safe for stack frames over 4 KiB on Windows: it omits the probe. Behavior is verified only on the tests below.

diagnosis.cause: the self-hosted general image backend omits the Windows guard-page probe for a large stack frame. The reference image starts the function at code offset 86,304 with `sub rsp, 0x1000; test byte [rsp], 0; sub rsp, 0xd38; test byte [rsp], 0`; the native image emits one `sub rsp, 0x1d38` instead. The probe pattern occurs once in the reference image and not at all in the native image (14 vs 13 `sub rsp, imm32` instructions). The extra bytes shift the rest of the image by 16 bytes after alignment, which is why a position-wise byte comparison reports 231 313 differences while the tail matches 99.5% under a 16-byte shift. A store/request/entry/target mismatch is ruled out because the author path reproduces the committed bytes from the same store and request.
diagnosis.reference: compiler/src/xax_x86_64.py `_reserve_stack` (line 184): for PE_HOSTED_IDENTITY and a frame over 4096 bytes it emits one `sub rsp, chunk; test byte [rsp], 0` per 4096-byte chunk; the self-hosted port does not implement that branch.
diagnosis.why_the_executor_matches: the committed executor store has 8 functions and rebuilds byte for byte through the same command; no probe difference arises in that program.
diagnosis.risk: the native-built server has not been shown to grow a > 4 KiB stack safely on Windows, because the guard-page touch is missing. It passed the test suite, but the two images are not equivalent in this respect.
diagnosis.upstream_fix: emit the same guard-page probe in the self-hosted backend (or make both builds agree on the threshold) so the same snapshot yields the same bytes, then commit a reproducible native compiler. Re-emitting the artifacts through the native layout instead would change the committed artifact hash and provenance. Either is an upstream decision; this repository keeps the author-built artifact as canonical and records the native build as a verified parity experiment.

not_done: the native-built server PE is not adopted as the canonical artifact and the committed 9f6e272b PE is unchanged; provenance equivalence between the two builds was not claimed
byte parity was measured for the two program stores here, not for arbitrary stores or targets

claim.label: EXECUTED
claim.statement: On this host the native Windows xaxc rebuilt at XAX 3e9b0c2 ran the PE stage of the build directly on both committed snapshot stores. It reproduced the 25 600 B executor PE byte for byte (6d563e0f...) in 53-65 ms, and produced a 359 424 B server PE (a87fdd10...) in 1.07-1.16 s that reports 0.8.0+native, pin 3e9b0c2b..., host contract r10 and python_on_request_path false, and passes every external test except the byte-identity assertion. The author path still reproduces the committed 9f6e272b... exactly from the same store. The two server images have the same size and identical imports; the only structural difference found is that the native build omits the reference build's Windows guard-page stack probe for a 0x1d38 stack frame, which shifts the rest of the image by 16 bytes and changes the relocated addresses. The open B1 item is fixing that omission and committing a native compiler, not the ability to build natively; the native-built artifact is not claimed safe for frames over 4 KiB on Windows.
